walkthroughs.body_html:
The Natural Environment — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Natural Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Natural Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

27 degrees

15 degrees

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.

mcqs.q: Why does the tropical rainforest have distinct vertical layers?
options: Rainforest layers exist because different animals live at different heights.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Competition for light: emergents (40m+), canopy (capturing most light), understorey (shade-tolerant) and forest floor (sparse vegetation due to low light) — each adapted to its light level.
Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
